mainTopic: Vegetable פאה, the hides of קדשים seized by powerful כהנים, and the four cries of the עזרה
overview: The גמרא first shows that the two ברייתות about פאה for vegetables hold only two opinions, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, who agree on the first vegetable. A ברייתא then tells of בן בוהיין, who gave פאה from vegetables. His father took the vegetables back and paid the poor double in tithed produce, because vegetables are not subject to פאה. Next, a ברייתא tells how powerful כהנים seized the hides of קדשים by force. Moving the division to ערב שבת did not stop them, so the owners consecrated the hides, and the money soon plated the whole היכל in gold. אבא שאול tells a similar story about the sycamore trunks of יריחו, and then a lament against four oppressive high-priestly families. A ברייתא lists four cries of the עזרה: two drove out unworthy כהנים (בני עלי and יששכר איש כפר ברקאי), and two welcomed worthy ones (ישמעאל בן פיאכי and יוחנן בן נרבאי). The amud ends as the גמרא begins the story of יששכר's punishment, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Are there three opinions on vegetable פאה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the two ברייתות show three different תנאים arguing about which vegetables get פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say there are three תנאים here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the two ברייתות it just quoted about which vegetables get פאה. It asks whether they add up to three separate opinions. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ברייתא has an anonymous תנא who lists two vegetables. Then רבי יוסי in one and רבי שמעון in the other each say 'אף' (also) and add a vegetable. Read simply, that looks like three different lists.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
The corner of the field left for the poor

phrases.english: Shall we say there are three Tannaim?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the two ברייתות on 56b about פאה for vegetables.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא תְּלָתָא תַּנָּאֵי הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion earlier on the ברייתות about vegetable פאה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the two ברייתות reflect three distinct opinions?

steps.title: Only two opinions: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the three-opinion reading. The anonymous תנא in each ברייתא is really the other named Sage.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, there are only two תנאים. The first תנא in רבי שמעון's ברייתא is רבי יוסי, and the first תנא in רבי יוסי's ברייתא is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says no, there are only two opinions. The 'anonymous' speaker in each ברייתא is simply the Sage named in the other ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The anonymous list in רבי שמעון's ברייתא is רבי יוסי's view. The anonymous list in רבי יוסי's ברייתא is רבי שמעון's view. This turns an apparent three-way argument into a two-way one. That raises a new problem with the word אף, which the next step solves.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (anonymous) Tanna in a ברייתא
That is / is the same as

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the anonymous תנא is a third person. In each ברייתא, the תנא קמא is the named Sage from the other ברייתא.

phrases.english: No, there are two Tannaim,
and the first Tanna before Rabbi Shimon
is Rabbi Yosei,
and the first Tanna before Rabbi Yosei
is Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, תְּרֵי תַּנָּאֵי הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of three opinions.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The three-opinion reading of the ברייתות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumes the anonymous תנא is a separate third authority.

steps.title: What 'אף' really refers to
steps.stepSummary: The word אף means they agree on the first vegetable, not that they add to the whole list.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'אף' (also)? It refers to the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word אף, which seemed to mean 'adding on.' It means the Sage agrees with the first vegetable on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each Sage is the anonymous voice of the other ברייתא, 'אף' cannot mean 'all of those plus mine.' Instead, both agree on the first vegetable, turnips. They argue only about the second vegetable, and each swaps in his own.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two opinions only. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון agree on the first vegetable and disagree on the second.

phrases.english: And what is 'also'? It refers to the first one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי ״אַף״ — אַקַּמַּיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem created by the answer in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אף means adding to the whole earlier list, which would imply three opinions.
steps.terutzMaskana: אף means agreeing only on the first vegetable.

steps.title: בן בוהיין gave פאה from vegetables
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: בן בוהיין gave vegetable פאה. His father took it back and gave the poor double in tithed produce, because the חכמים say there is no פאה for vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: בן בוהיין gave פאה from vegetables. His father came and found poor people loaded with vegetables, standing at the garden's entrance. He said to them: 'My sons, throw them off, and I will give you double in tithed produce. Not because I am stingy, but because the חכמים said: one does not give פאה from vegetables.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a story connected to the topic of vegetable פאה. A father undoes his son's mistaken gift of פאה and pays the poor back double.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real פאה is exempt from מעשר. Vegetables are not subject to פאה, so these vegetables were not true פאה, and they still needed to be tithed. The father kept the poor from eating untithed food (טבל) and made sure they lost nothing by giving them double, already tithed.

keyTerms.meaning: I am stingy (literally, 'my eye is narrow')

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows in practice that vegetables are not subject to פאה, so anything given that way still needs to be tithed.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The son of Bohayan gave peah from vegetables,
and his father came and found the poor
who were loaded with vegetables
and standing at the entrance of the garden.
He said to them: My sons, throw them off yourselves
and I will give you double in tithed produce.
Not because I am stingy,
but because the Sages said:
One does not give peah from vegetables.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בֶּן בּוּהְיָין נָתַן פֵּיאָה לַיָּרָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on the same theme of vegetable פאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vegetables are not subject to פאה, so vegetables given as פאה still require tithing.

steps.title: Why did the father say he was not stingy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the father needed to add 'not because I am stingy.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did he need to tell them, 'not because I am stingy'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about one extra line in the story. It sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offering double payment already showed his generosity. So the extra sentence seems unnecessary, and the גמרא wants to know what it adds.

phrases.english: Why did he need to say to them
'Not because I am stingy'?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימְרָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the ברייתא of step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the extra phrase 'not because I am stingy.'

steps.title: So the poor would not think he was brushing them off
steps.stepSummary: He said it so the poor would not suspect he was pushing them away and would never pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that they would not say: 'He is just putting us off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the father wanted to reassure the poor. He did not want them to think his promise was an empty excuse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor might suspect he took the vegetables now and would never give the double payment. Stating his real reason, a ruling of the חכמים, made his promise believable.

phrases.english: So that they would not say:
He is putting us off.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לֵימְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To prevent the poor from suspecting that his promise was a way to get rid of them.

steps.title: Strong כהנים grabbed the hides of קדשים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the hides of קדשים were stored in לשכת בית הפרוה and divided in the evening, but strong כהנים took them by force.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: At first, they would put the hides of קדשים in לשכת בית הפרוה. In the evening they divided them among the men of the בית אב, and the strong ones would take them by force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא connected to the theme of strong people taking by force, like the people who took wood from יריחו. It describes a problem in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each day's בית אב split the hides among its own members. That was a small group, so powerful כהנים could bully the others and grab the hides.

keyTerms.meaning: Hides of sacrificial animals (given to the כהנים)
The Parva chamber in the בית המקדש
The priestly family on duty that day

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: At first,
they would place the hides of consecrated animals
in the chamber of Beit HaParva;
in the evening they would distribute them
to the men of the family on duty.
And the strong-armed men would
take them by force.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין עוֹרוֹת קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא with the theme of powerful people taking by force.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The original daily division of hides was abused by powerful כהנים.

steps.title: The fix: divide the hides every ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים made a תקנה to divide the hides weekly on ערב שבת, when both משמרות were present together.
steps.simpleTranslation: They enacted that the hides be divided from ערב שבת to ערב שבת, because then all the משמרות came and took them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by telling how the חכמים solved the problem. They moved the division to ערב שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב שבת, the outgoing משמר and the incoming משמר were both in the בית המקדש. With so many כהנים present at once, the strong ones could no longer grab the hides.
steps.whatToRemember: The תקנה used a large crowd on ערב שבת to stop the bullying by powerful כהנים.

phrases.english: They enacted that they should distribute them
from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve,
when all the watches come,
and take them together.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מְחַלְּקִין אוֹתָן מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the solution to the problem described in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hides are divided weekly on ערב שבת, in the presence of both משמרות.

steps.title: The powerful still grabbed the hides, so the owners consecrated them
steps.stepSummary: Even after the weekly division, the leading כהנים still took the hides by force, so the owners of the קרבנות consecrated the hides to הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the important כהנים still took the hides by force. So the owners of the sacrifices got up and consecrated the hides to Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story from Step 8. The weekly תקנה did not solve the problem, so the owners found a new solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With both משמרות present, the plain grabbing stopped, but the גדולי כהונה still used their status to take the hides. Once the owners made the hides הקדש, no כהן could keep them. Grabbing them now would mean stealing from הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The owners (here, the people who brought the sacrifices)
They consecrated them to Heaven, making them Temple property

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the owners were punishing the כהנים for no reason. The hides were no longer reaching the ordinary כהנים fairly. Giving them to הקדש took them away from the people who were abusing them.

phrases.english: And still the prominent priests
would take them by force.
The owners arose
and consecrated them to Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲדַיִין הָיוּ גְּדוֹלֵי כְהוּנָּה נוֹטְלִין אוֹתָן בִּזְרוֹעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the תקנה from Step 8 was not enough, which leads to a stronger solution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the powerful כהנים kept seizing the hides, the owners consecrated them to הקדש so no one could seize them.

steps.title: The consecrated hides paid for gold plating on the Sanctuary
steps.stepSummary: Within a short time, money from the consecrated hides covered the entire היכל in gold tablets. These were shown to the pilgrims on the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: only a few days passed before they covered the whole היכל with gold tablets. Each tablet was one אמה by one אמה, as thick as a gold דינר. On the festival they would fold them up and put them on a step on the הר הבית, so the pilgrims could see that the work was beautiful and had no flaw.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells the result of consecrating the hides. The money was so large that it quickly paid to plate the whole היכל in gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how much value the powerful כהנים had been taking for themselves. Once that value went to הקדש, it quickly paid for gold plating. Showing the tablets to the עולי רגלים let the public see that the work was beautiful and flawless.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building of the בית המקדש
A gold coin, used here as a measure of thickness
Pilgrims who came up to ירושלים for the festivals

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the scale of the corruption. The hides stolen by force were worth enough to cover the whole היכל in gold.

phrases.english: They said: only a few days passed
before they plated the entire Sanctuary
with tablets of gold,
which were a cubit by a cubit
as thick as a gold dinar,
and at the Festival they would fold them up

phrases.aramaic: וּמַנִּיחִין אוֹתָן עַל גַּב מַעֲלָה בְּהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: and place them on a step on the Temple Mount,
so that the pilgrims would see
that their workmanship was beautiful and had no flaw.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: לֹא הָיוּ יָמִים מוּעָטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the outcome of the consecration in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The value of the consecrated hides quickly paid to plate the whole היכל in gold.

steps.title: A parallel story: sycamore trunks in Jericho
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול teaches a similar case. Strong men seized sycamore trunks in יריחו by force, so the owners consecrated them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: אבא שאול says, there were sycamore trunks in יריחו. Strong-armed people would take them by force. So the owners got up and consecrated them to Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא with the same pattern. Powerful people grabbed property, so the owners made it הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the hides, the trunks were being taken by force. The owners used the same defense: they made the trunks Temple property, so the strong men could not take them. This also explains why the sycamore trees of יריחו (mentioned earlier in the sugya) were הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Trunks or beams of sycamore trees

phrases.english: It was taught: Abba Shaul says:
There were sycamore trunks in Jericho,
and powerful people
would take them by force,
so the owners arose and consecrated them to Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא, אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case with the same pattern as Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Owners whose sycamore trunks were seized by force consecrated them to הקדש.

steps.title: The lament against the corrupt high-priestly families
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול בן בטנית, quoting אבא יוסף בן חנין, cries "woe is me" about four high-priestly families and the way each one oppressed the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: About them, and people like them, אבא שאול בן בטנית said in the name of אבא יוסף בן חנין: Woe is me from the house of ביתוס, woe from their clubs. Woe is me from the house of חנין, woe from their whispering. Woe is me from the house of קתרוס, woe from their pens. Woe is me from the house of ישמעאל בן פיאכי, woe from their fists.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the stories of grabbing by force to a famous lament about powerful high-priestly families.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each family is named together with its weapon. One used clubs. One used whispered slander. One used pens to write false decrees. One used fists. Together they show the different ways power was abused: physical force, rumors, and false writing.

phrases.english: About them and those like them
Abba Shaul ben Batnit said
in the name of Abba Yosef ben Ḥanin:
Woe is me from the house of Baitos —
woe is me from their clubs,
woe is me from the house of Ḥanin —
woe is me from their whispering,
woe is me from the house of Katros —
woe is me from their pens,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹי לִי מִבֵּית יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן פִּיאָכִי —
phrases.english: woe is me from the house of Yishmael ben Piakhi —
woe is me from their fists.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲלֵיהֶם וְעַל כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶם אָמַר אַבָּא שָׁאוּל בֶּן בָּטְנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the theme of taking by force (Steps 9 and 11) to bring a broader lament about abuse of power.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four high-priestly families are condemned, each for its own method of oppression.

steps.title: Why these families had so much power
steps.stepSummary: Their power came from controlling the whole Temple system: the fathers were כהנים גדולים, the sons treasurers, the sons-in-law overseers, and their servants beat the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: For they were כהנים גדולים, their sons were treasurers, their sons-in-law were overseers, and their servants beat the people with sticks.
steps.whatsHappening: The lament ends by explaining why no one could stand up to these families. They held every key position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The family filled every level of authority: high priesthood, treasury (גזברים), and administration (אמרכלים). With their servants enforcing their will, the people had no one to complain to. This explains why the owners in Steps 9 and 11 had to turn to הקדש for protection.
steps.whatToRemember: When the powerful kept seizing the hides (and the Jericho trunks), the owners consecrated them to הקדש. The value was enough to plate the היכל in gold. The גמרא closes with a lament over the high-priestly families who held every position of power and oppressed the people.

phrases.english: For they were High Priests,
and their sons were treasurers,
and their sons-in-law were overseers,
and their servants beat the people with sticks.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהֵם כֹּהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source of the power behind the lament in Step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: These families controlled every level of Temple authority, so the people could not resist their abuses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These families held the high priesthood, the treasury and the administration, and their servants beat the people, so no one could stand up to them.

steps.title: The courtyard cried four cries; the first drove out the sons of Eli
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the עזרה cried four cries. The first was against בני עלי, who defiled the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: The Temple courtyard cried out four cries. The first: 'Leave here, sons of עלי, who made the Sanctuary of ה׳ impure!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists four 'cries' of the עזרה. It starts with the first one, against בני עלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of the previous steps, which described כהנים who abused their power. The ברייתא shows that even the Temple itself 'protested' against unworthy כהנים. The first example comes from the time of נביאים: בני עלי, whose sins defiled the Sanctuary.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of עלי the כהן גדול (חפני and פנחס), who sinned in the משכן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse פנחס בן עלי, one of the sinful בני עלי here, with the righteous פנחס בן אלעזר who is mentioned in the third cry.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The Temple courtyard cried four cries.
phrases.notes: The people gathered in the עזרה cried out together, so it is as if the courtyard itself cried.

phrases.english: The first: Leave here, sons of Eli,
who defiled the Sanctuary of ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַרְבַּע צְווֹחוֹת צָוְחָה עֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of corrupt כהנים from the 'woe is me' passage with a new ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עזרה cried four cries; the first expelled בני עלי for defiling the היכל.

steps.title: The second cry drove out יששכר איש כפר ברקאי, who served with silk-wrapped hands
steps.stepSummary: The second cry was against יששכר איש כפר ברקאי, who honored himself and disgraced holy things. The גמרא explains that he wrapped his hands in silk while doing the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it cried again: 'Leave here, יששכר of Kfar Barkai, who honors himself and disgraces the holy things of Heaven!' For he would wrap his hands in silk and then do the עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the second cry, against יששכר איש כפר ברקאי. The גמרא adds a short explanation of what he did wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His sin was that he cared more about his own comfort than about the honor of the עבודה. He would not let his hands get dirty from the קרבנות. The silk also came between his hands and the holy vessels, which is a חציצה, so his עבודה was not proper.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול from the village of Kfar Barkai
Honors himself, puts his own dignity first
Disgraces the holy things of Heaven

phrases.english: And it cried again:

phrases.aramaic: צֵא מִיכָּן יִשָּׂשׂכָר אִישׁ כְּפַר בַּרְקַאי
phrases.english: Leave here, Yissakhar of Kfar Barkai,
who honors himself
and disgraces the holy things of Heaven.
For he would wrap his hands in silk
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's Aramaic explanation of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and perform the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד צָוְוחָה: צֵא מִיכָּן יִשָּׂשׂכָר אִישׁ כְּפַר בַּרְקַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second of the four cries, again a cry of expulsion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יששכר איש כפר ברקאי was cried out of the Temple for serving with silk-wrapped hands, putting his own honor above the honor of the קדשים.

steps.title: The third cry welcomed ישמעאל בן פיאכי as כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The third cry was positive. It called on the gates to open so that ישמעאל בן פיאכי, a student of פנחס, could enter and serve as כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the courtyard cried again: 'Lift up your heads, O gates, and let ישמעאל בן פיאכי, the student of פנחס, enter and serve as כהן גדול!'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now changes direction. Instead of driving someone out, the עזרה welcomes a worthy כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'Lift up your heads, O gates' come from תהלים כד, a call of welcome and honor. Calling him a 'student of פנחס' means he followed the path of the zealous, righteous פנחס בן אלעזר. This is so even though his family name appears among the oppressive families in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Lift up your heads, O gates (תהלים כד), a welcoming call
A student, meaning a follower, of פנחס בן אלעזר

phrases.english: And the courtyard cried again:
Lift up your heads, O gates,
and let Yishmael ben Piakhi enter,
the student of Pinchas,
and serve as High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד צָוְוחָה הָעֲזָרָה: שְׂאוּ שְׁעָרִים רָאשֵׁיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from cries of expulsion to cries of welcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עזרה welcomed ישמעאל בן פיאכי as a worthy כהן גדול.

steps.title: The fourth cry welcomed יוחנן בן נרבאי to eat the offerings
steps.stepSummary: The fourth cry welcomed יוחנן בן נרבאי, a student of פנקאי, to come in and fill his belly with the holy offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the courtyard cried again: 'Lift up your heads, O gates, and let יוחנן בן נרבאי, the student of פנקאי, enter and fill his belly with the holy offerings of Heaven!'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the fourth and last cry, another welcome. This time it is for יוחנן בן נרבאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating the meat of קרבנות is itself a מצוה for כהנים. Here, 'filling his belly' is said as praise: he was worthy of eating קדשים and did it fully. The next step explains why this was so valuable.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול praised for eating the offerings

steps.confusionAlert: 'Fill his belly with holy offerings' sounds like an insult about gluttony, but here it is praise. It is a cry of welcome, just like the third cry, and step 18 shows that his eating made sure no holy meat went to waste.

phrases.english: And the courtyard cried again:
Lift up your heads, O gates,
and let Yochanan ben Narbai enter,
the student of Pinkai,
and fill his belly with the holy offerings of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד צָוְוחָה הָעֲזָרָה: שְׂאוּ שְׁעָרִים רָאשֵׁיכֶם וְיִכָּנֵס יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נִרְבַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels the third cry with a second welcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עזרה welcomed יוחנן בן נרבאי to eat the קדשים.

steps.title: יוחנן בן נרבאי's huge meals meant no נותר
steps.stepSummary: יוחנן בן נרבאי and his household ate 300 calves, drank 300 jugs of wine, and ate 40 סאה of young birds for dessert. In all his days, no נותר was found in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about יוחנן בן נרבאי that he would eat three hundred calves, drink three hundred jugs of wine, and eat forty סאה of young birds as dessert. They said: In all the days of יוחנן בן נרבאי, no leftover sacrificial meat was found in the Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the fourth cry by describing how much יוחנן בן נרבאי ate. It shows the good result: holy meat was never left over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat of a קרבן that is not eaten in time becomes נותר and must be burned, which wastes holy food. Because יוחנן בן נרבאי made sure every bit was eaten, there was never any נותר. That is why 'filling his belly' was praise.

keyTerms.meaning: Dessert, the end of the meal
Sacrificial meat left past its time, which must be burned

steps.whatToRemember: Two cries expelled unworthy כהנים (בני עלי, יששכר) and two welcomed worthy ones (ישמעאל בן פיאכי, יוחנן בן נרבאי). יוחנן's praise was that no קדשים ever became נותר in his days.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נִרְבַּאי
phrases.english: They said about Yochanan ben Narbai
that he would eat three hundred calves,
phrases.notes: That's counting him together with his household.

phrases.english: and drink three hundred jugs of wine,
and eat forty se'ah of young birds
as dessert.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: כׇּל יָמָיו שֶׁל יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נִרְבַּאי
phrases.english: They said: All the days of Yochanan ben Narbai
no leftover sacrificial meat was found in the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נִרְבַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and expands on the fourth cry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of יוחנן בן נרבאי's eating, no נותר was ever found in the מקדש during his days.

steps.title: What finally happened to יששכר איש כפר ברקאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the second cry and asks what happened in the end to יששכר איש כפר ברקאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: What happened in the end to יששכר of Kfar Barkai?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to יששכר from the second cry and asks how his story ended. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said he was driven out. Now the גמרא wants to know his final punishment, which will match his sin of disrespecting the קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: What became of him? What was his end?

phrases.english: What became of
Yissakhar of Kfar Barkai?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי סְלִקָא בֵּיהּ בְּיִשָּׂשׂכָר אִישׁ כְּפַר בַּרְקַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from יוחנן בן נרבאי to the second cry about יששכר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final outcome or punishment of יששכר איש כפר ברקאי.

steps.title: The king and queen argue whether goat or lamb is better, and summon the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: A king and queen argued: he said goat meat is better, she said lamb meat. They decided the כהן גדול could settle it, since he offers קרבנות every day. יששכר came. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: A king and queen were sitting together. The king said, 'Goat is better.' The queen said, 'Lamb is better.' They said, 'Who can prove it? The כהן גדול, since he offers sacrifices every day.' He came,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the question by telling a story. This step only sets the scene: the argument, and יששכר being called. The ending comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול could take a portion from any קרבן, so he would know the taste of every kind of meat. The setup is ironic: the man who treated the עבודה like his own private comfort is now asked to judge holy offerings by how they taste.

keyTerms.meaning: Who can prove it? Who can decide?

phrases.english: They said: The king and the queen were sitting.
The king said: Goat is better,
and the queen said: Lamb is better.
They said: Who can prove it?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, דְּקָא מַסֵּיק קׇרְבָּנוֹת כׇּל יוֹמָא.
phrases.english: The High Priest, since he offers sacrifices every day.
He came,
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: מַלְכָּא וּמַלְכְּתָא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question about יששכר's fate.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer begins with a story: the king and queen summoned יששכר, the כהן גדול, to settle their argument about goat versus lamb. His response and punishment follow on the next amud.
